subject: Access provenance: service-account rotation exception & SCIM sample request
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthsync.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: security-assessments@healthsync.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: rotation logs, SCIM delta & SAML assertion samples for SOC2/SIG

Hi Olga,

We’re kicking off our SIG/SOC2 assessment for the access control domain and have a few targeted asks around service accounts and provisioning evidence. Can you provide the following by end of next week (May 28):

- Service account rotation logs for Q1 2026 (rotation timestamps, actor, key id)
- Any documented rotation-exception tickets (security-approved extended key lifetimes) for service accounts in scope
- SCIM delta export for April 2026 (created/updated/deleted events) — CSV preferred
- 3–5 SAML assertion samples for interactive SSO and one for an automated service flow (include timestamps)

We try to avoid full PII in artifacts; redact email addresses where possible but keep object ids and timestamps intact. If anything needs a longer lead time, please flag. We can use a shared Drive folder (we'll share a secure link) or send via your preferred secure exchange.

Also, quick confirmation: do you use ephemeral tokens/JIT admin for on-demand elevated actions or do you rely mainly on long-lived service-account keys?

Thanks,
Emily
Security Assessment Manager
HealthSync
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthsync.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: rotation logs, SCIM delta & SAML assertion samples for SOC2/SIG

Emily — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marcus (ownership for infra/service accounts) and Tessa (IAM & provisioning) to assemble the package. Plan below:

- We'll prepare CSV extracts and sample SAML assertions.
- Expect preliminary artifacts by Tue 2026-05-25; final, redacted bundle by Fri 2026-05-28.
- We’ll include exception tickets and a short narrative describing rotation cadence and who approves exceptions.

Quick answers to your token question: we use a mix — ephemeral tokens (short-lived) for human/JIT elevation, but some automation still runs with long-lived keys that are rotated per policy. Marcus will call out which accounts remain as long-lived and provide justification/ticket references.

Where would you like us to drop the files? We can upload to the Drive folder in your email or provide a secure S3 bundle and a presigned link.

Cheers,
Olga
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthsync.com>
Cc: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: rotation logs, SCIM delta & SAML assertion samples for SOC2/SIG

Emily / Olga — attached the requested artifacts (redaction applied where emails would expose PII):

Attachments (stubs):
- scim_delta_apr2026.csv (columns: object_id, op, attr_changed, actor_id, timestamp)
- svcacct_rotation_Q1_2026.csv (columns: svcacct_id, rotation_ts, rotated_by, key_id, method)
- exception_ticket_1427.pdf (rotation extension approved 2026-03-11; approver: security@redwood.com)
- saml_assertion_samples_202605.txt (5 samples: 4 interactive SSO, 1 automation flow)

Notes:
- The svcacct_rotation file includes rotations performed by CI automation and manual rotations; we tag manual rotations with ticket references.
- Exception ticket 1427 corresponds to a legacy monitoring service that temporarily required extended key lifetime; ticket contains approval thread and compensating controls.
- Ephemeral/JIT: we use short-lived OIDC tokens via our internal gateway for human elevated sessions. Service workflows that cannot tolerate ephemeral creds are scoped to dedicated service accounts with quarterly rotation.
- Retention policy: rotation logs and SCIM deltas are retained for 13 months for audit purposes.

If you need additional sample assertions for a particular tenant or timestamp, say which timestamp range and we’ll pull those specifically.

— Marcus
Sr. Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@healthsync.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: security-assessments@healthsync.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: rotation logs, SCIM delta & SAML assertion samples for SOC2/SIG

Marcus/Olga — received, thank you. I spot-checked the SCIM CSV and rotation log; format looks good. Two quick follow-ups:

1) For the exception ticket, can you also include the compensating-controls checklist that was referenced in the approval email? We need to map the compensating controls to SIG sub-controls.
2) For the SAML assertion automation sample, can you confirm the audience and the NameID format used in the assertion (we saw transient in the interactive samples but need a persistent identifier for the automation flow).

If you can drop the compensating-controls checklist as a short PDF and annotate the automation assertion sample with a single-line comment identifying the fields, that would close our asks.

Best,
Emily
Security Assessment Manager
HealthSync
